atlas.title: Historical atlas
atlas.intro: Archaeological cultures and historical states of South Asia, on a historical time axis only. Stories and cosmic ages never appear here: those live in the cosmic and epic modes.
atlas.historyOnly: Historical years only. Narrative events and cosmic ages are never placed on this axis.
atlas.mapLabel: Map of historical sites and the approximate reach of historical states
atlas.reachNote: Approximate reach based on {count, plural, one {# attested site} other {# attested sites}}
atlas.reachExplain: Shaded areas are drawn around places where inscriptions, coins or excavations attest a state. They are not borders: ancient states had no surveyed frontiers, and their influence shifted over time.
atlas.none: Nothing recorded for this period yet.
atlas.empty: Historical periods have not been added yet.

civ.title: Civilisation atlas
civ.intro: How stories and traditions travelled. Each tradition is its own branch; each link between them says what kind of connection the sources support, from a documented direct borrowing to an open hypothesis.
civ.nations: Modern countries are shown only to help you find places. No modern nation is presented as the heir or extension of an ancient state or tradition.
civ.empty: Transmissions have not been added yet.
civ.directExplain: A documented borrowing: the later work draws on the earlier one.
civ.shared_ancestryExplain: Both descend from a common older source rather than one from the other.
civ.reinterpretationExplain: The story was retold and reshaped to fit another tradition's values.
civ.independent_similarityExplain: The two resemble each other, but there is no evidence of contact.
civ.uncertain_hypothesisExplain: Scholars propose a connection but disagree, or the evidence is thin.

history.evidenceSitesNote: Places where inscriptions, coins or excavations attest this state. The map draws its approximate reach from these.
